Having made a successful landing a spaceman disembarks and the player directs him to collect boxes that are on the planet surface. The aliens are understandably hostile and will pursue and shoot the spaceman if they can. The game is customizable. Music can be turned on or off, there are three levels of difficulty, and the number of lives available can be set from 1 to 8. The game has a 'hot-seat' two-player mode. Player one goes first and scores as many points as possible with their first life. Then player two takes over until they too lose their first life, after which its back to player one. This continues until both players have used up all their lives.

154349.overview: In Haunted House, players control a ghost who has the task of preventing 20 souls from escaping the haunted house. They arrive in a room with eight doors, with the soul coming out from one of them. They must try to capture the souls before they reach the key that sits in the middle of the room and walking into the vortex nearby. If the souls fall into the vortex before the player captures them, then the player must go in after the souls. The vortex leads to the maze, and the object here is to try and capture the souls before they enter another vortex, while avoiding snakes and crashing into walls. Once players have captured 20 souls, the game's difficulty increases with bats appearing in the main room and speed increases.

154450.overview: In Galivan (released by Imagine in the US as Hero 2020) the player takes the role of the last remaining member of the Cosmo Police. His comrades died while trying to free the planet Cynep from the evil roaming on it. Now the player is the last hope. This game is a mix between a shooter and a platformer: the player walks through the caves, jumps over obstacles and shoots everything in sight. Well, at least if he has a weapon: at the beginning he is unarmed and can only kick or punch. He has to find pyramids which were dropped by his dead colleagues (also sometimes from killed aliens): those grant an armor, more life energy and a weapon. When the player find even another pyramid, the weapon gets upgraded for a limited amount of time. However, every hit decreases the life energy and if it goes down too far, the armor and weapon are lost. Reaching zero results in death. At the end of every level, the player has to defeat a big boss alien.

154468.overview: Six different track and field disciplines are recreated in this multi-event sports simulation. Up to six human players can take them on.You can replay each attempt, or watch simulated recording of the world record distances and speeds of the day, for training purposes. 100m sprint and 110m hurdles have a similar joystick waggling technique, but time the jumps over the hurdles accurately. The long jump is also waggling-based, with the joystick being pushed up to launch the jump and ensure a correct landing. In diving you can choose the jump to attempt, with more difficult ones worth more points if you get it right. In archery you shoot at four circles of differing distances several times, aiming to get as close to the centre as possible. This is done by holding down fire to prepare the arrow, and push down to release the bow. Weightlifting involves the snatch and clean-and-jerk phases, with the latter involving more joystick presses to keep the weights under control.

155519.overview:
Galencia is a game developed in 2017 by Jason Aldred and published by Protovision. It is heavily inspired by the 80s arcade smash hit Galaga.

The game has 50 waves (levels) for you to complete. It won the 2017 Game of the year from Reset64 Magazine. A modified version called Galancia Mini was released for free on the December 2018 firmware update for the C64 Mini.

From Protovision's website:

EARTH, 2017.

We didn't listen to the warnings.

We decided to ignore the decline of our bee population,and now their guardians have arrived.

You must pilot the 1981 Galencia Fighter and restore order. Before its too late!

156310.overview: Gala is a horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up. Based on the Chris Yates Galax-i-Birds game released by Firebird in that same year, but with modified sprites.

156701.overview: This game from 1987 is based on the adventures of the French comic book character Iznogoud. You are in the role of the Grand Vizier Iznogoud, whose only thought is to depose the Caliph of magical Baghdad and become "Caliph instead of the Caliph!" To accomplish this aim, you must wander around and interact with characters around you, acquiring objects along the way that may or may not be useful, and figure out how all this will help you achieve your goal. During the game, you have 4 different methods of interacting with other characters: you can give objects to them, you can threaten them, you can flatter them, and you can throw a tantrum. Depending on the character, these actions will elicit different responses--or none altogether. You will need objects for various things, and objects are all acquired from other characters. Some characters are helpful, others are not. But the right combination of your actions will help you to become Caliph instead of the Caliph, while the wrong ones will often land you in a cell beneath the palace. Just be careful not to lose your own head in the process!

156891.overview:
The original arcade game with all complete 8 levels was developed as fan project for the C64 by the group Nostalgia in 2015. 
              * Two completely new levels added
              * Existing 4 levels are twice the size
              * All levels with completely new gfx
              * Each level has a new unique tune
              * Each boss fight has a new tune
              * New Sound Effects added or changed
              * New bug free sprite multiplexer
               * Intro sequence added 
              * Game Map added
              * Game Completed Animation added
              * Game Over sequence added
              * Two new bosses added for levels 5 & 6
              * New Jumping Skeleten Enemy added
              * Moving Clouds completely recoded
             * Arthur can now turn around while jumping so he can shoot backwards
              * Arthur can jump over obstacles when he is touching them
              * Weapon system improved
              * Enemies have improved AI and a lot of  them are completely recoded
              * Hitting an enemy animation added
              * Time Limit is much better and fairer
              * Title Screen with Title Tune added
               * Pause added with Quit option
              * Easyflash version with High Score saver to flash and backup to disk
              * Universal File version that should work on any device
              * IFFL version with REU support
              * PAL and NTSC supported

156965.overview:
A strategy game, created by Markus Schneider and published in Golden Disk 64 1991/05. GILDED AGE- Take on the role of a Northern General fighting the armies of the South in this gripping strategy game! Do extensive research into a historical tactical game that also contains a lot of action.
Tons of mesmerizing graphics and realistic battle sounds make this game a real hit! There are many different action areas for the player to choose from: building an army, attacking Native Americans. Train robberies, duels, etc.

157301.overview:
Jukebox is a musical strategy game that's kind of a cross between a chess match and a dance contest. During the game the Jukebox is jumpin' with lots of terrific songs. Songs so good you never want them to stop. But to keep the music playing you've got to create gold records. Using your dancing feet and your natural sense of rhythm you jump from square to square creating hit records as you go. Aim for the pulsating gold tiles, because you can build them into records. And the more gold records you get the more coins you earn. Use the coins to keep the music bopping and the game from stopping. Play against the computer or another player. 
But plan your strategy carefully, because in Jukebox you can box yourself in - and then the music's over.

157421.overview:
Go is a computer implementation of the classic board game.

Played on a 19 x 19 grid, it allows for 2-player competitive or 1-player versus computer play. Players take turns placing either a black or a white marker on the screen, with the goal to capture the opponent's piece by surrounding it in the 4 cardinal directions. The winner is the player with the most captured pieces after the board is filled. The player can set a computer handicap which allows them to start with 0 - 9 friendly pieces on the board.

158503.overview:
Time to get your bat and pads, put on the whites and have a game of cricket. In this computer version of the game, you have the choice of length of game (40, 50, 60 overs or two innings), how many players (one or two), skill level (one to nine) and whether you want to play a simulation or arcade version. You then choose your eleven players for each team: wicket-keepers, slip catchers and bowlers.

The main game is viewed showing a small part of the field from behind the bowler at an elevated angle. Also shown: the batters, wicket-keeper and slip catcher. In simulation mode you control the direction of the ball when bowling. In arcade you can determine the speed as well. For the batter, in simulation mode you can play defensively or aggressively. In arcade mode you always play aggressively. If a ball is hit into the field then it shows a side view at an elevated angle of the fielders chasing the ball. The computer determines how many runs you get.

158504.overview: Bridge, the card game. This is a trick-taking card game for four players who form two partnerships, or "sides". The partners on each side sit opposite one another. Game play is in two phases: bidding and playing

159372.overview: Lawn Tennis (re-released as "Grand Prix Tennis" by MAD) allows you to play against the computer or another player in a five set game of tennis. The court is shown on the whole screen at an isometric angle and all the rules and scoring follows the actual game of tennis closely. There are five skill levels that can be selected at the start of the game (one - five).

159564.overview:
Golf Master is a golf game where you can play a full round of golf on one course solo or with up to three friends. Before you play there are various options that can be selected. There are three levels of ability, Novice, Amateur or Professional which affects the strength of the wind. If you want to play in a competition between yourself or with friends, or practice on any hole. Lastly you can select how many holes or which holes to play. 1-18, 1-9, 10-18 or on one hole from the 18.

The game itself is a top-down view showing a part of the course. Holding down the Space Bar scrolls the screen showing the rest of the course. You now have various options to select your shot. You can choose your club, the direction and power of the shot. Once happy with your selection you don't actually play the shot but just watch a little animation of the shot being taken. If you are playing with friends you actually have to wait for each player to complete the hole, not after each shot like in real golf.

The game was re-released by Prism Leisure Corporation in 1992 under the name Challenge Golf (on the boxart only, the game still had the Golf Master name on the title screen).

159616.overview:
Scalextric is a brand of slot cars and  Hornby slot care racing system sets which first appeared in the late 1950s. This game brought that to life in first person for the fans of the brand, though this was good enough that it was also released as Gran Prix later in Europe. 

European version / Radio Elettronica & Computer 1987/12 (Anno XVI Numero 10) / a.k.a. "Grand Prix". Released in North America as Slot Car Racer. 

The game is a simple two car, split screen racing game. Cars cannot come off the track but they do lose speed when driving along the track edge or when skidding in the chicanes.

Cars can crash, a crash is when one car hits another from behind at a speed that's in excess of 20 mph. In a crash such as this the car that's behind automatically loses the race. However if the cars are level the race does allow one driver to move sideways to push the other player out of the way, either to make passing easier or to distract the other player.

Each race can be for one or two players and when racing against the computer the player an select one of three difficulty levels to play against. Races can be from 1 to 99 laps long and the player has a choice of racing on one of the 2 supplied circuits or they can design their own.

The C64 version of the game was released as Slot Car Racers in North America.

159993.overview: Gridder is a single screen game played over an 8 x 8 grid where you control a head and you have to fill in all the boxes to complete a level. As you move around the grid you paint the lines and when a box has been surrounded then it fills in. Scorpions also move around the screen and they must be avoided because if you touch one then you lose one of three lives. If you complete a level before the timer reaches zero then you receive bonus points.

160147.overview: 500cc Grand Prix is a motorbike simulator viewed from behind your bike. It lets you ride on 12 circuits all around the world. You can play either alone or against a friend (with an unusual vertically-split screen), and in addition to the championship mode (9 laps with 6 competitors) there's a training mode (just 2 laps with 2 competitors). You can chose to race on any circuit at a time or go for the world championship mode where you race on the circuits in order.

160313.overview: Gnom Yet another Norwegian strategy game. Follow the Gnomen in thick and thin! Facing dangers and challenges with family and friends. A real challenge for more than your fingertips! Try combination skills and logic along the way with the Gnomen.

160329.overview:
Avoid the ghosts and collect up the shiny gold. Gold is dug for on the playing field next to the main road, which then has to be brought to the site.
The game begins after a 6 is rolled. The computer takes over the rolling of the dice for the whole game. Before proceeding, you have to buy something in field A: food by entering a number from 1-9. Note: the higher the number, the greater the food and thus longer endurance on the long trail - but also slower progress. Because you also have to look for gold and pick it up. The additional equipment with tool is entered by entering a 0 or 1 = yes or no. Note: without this equipment, interruptions on the road cannot be overcome. You can dig for gold on both sides of the pathThe player's progress is determined by rolling the randomly generated dice.  

When digging, the player finds gold or a chest, also with gold or with an event (poisonous snake, robber). Collected gold pieces are credited to the points account. These finds are only certain in the bank (on field B). This field can only be reached directly for redemption, otherwise it will be returned. Breaks on the road can only be overcome with the additional equipment. The game ends when players are "starved" or have been dug everywhere. The game is played with a joystick and release button. 

Hints: The more a player carries (gold, provisions, equipment), the slower he progresses. If two players reach the opposing field directly, they are caught and you get your gold. You can be walk in both directions.

160334.overview: German golf game for up to six players. It was part of a double game pack along with a bowling game.

160337.overview:
Endorsed by famous tennis player, Jimmy Connors, this game offers tournament and single play on multiple court types.

Using crosshairs, aim your ball to the other side of the court and hope you hit where you want. If you are lucky, you might even score an Ace. If not, you will need to be ready to return your opponent's return. Run back and forth as you try to keep hitting the ball over the net until your opponent misses, or you do. When you hit the ball, you will want to attempt changing the direction and speed of the ball to throw your opponent off balance. This is the real challenge of any tennis game.

162687.overview: Get Spectre! Before he gets us! You are our top agent on your toughest assignment yet. A cunning and ruthless enemy hit man is somewhere in Europe, out to liquidate your network. using intelligence reports (sometimes in code), timetables and computerized maps, you must meet Control's challenge to keep your Super Agent rating.

162847.overview: Adventure 2: The Great Pyramid, like its predecessor, is a text adventure game with little to no story. The aim in the game is to find a number of treasures that are scattered around the game world. The world comprises a great pyramid and its immediate surrounding desert. The game features save and restore functionality.

163775.overview:
Only you can save the world from destruction, by finding four parts of the weapon to use against the Alien Syndicate's evil leader. This task must be completed within 80 minutes, although you have five lives available.

Gameplay mainly involves propelling your jumpsuit-backed and powerfully-armed character through the levels, destroying the alien forces as he goes. The levels have lots of pieces of ledges and spikes all around, which must be planned around, as well as lava pits. There is extra weaponry and ammunition to collect along the way. Your main weapon can be fired in any direction, but you can't move and fire at the same time, unless you're firing to the left or right.

163953.overview:
Help Grunio, a guinea pig, eat all the carrots in this retro mini game for Commodore 64!
Gruniozerca is a Commodore 64 version of NES/Famicom mini game released in 2016. Both games were created to support Polish 24h charity games stream called Gramytatywnie.

Use joystick connected to port 2 to move Grunio on the screen and catch all carrots before they touch the ground. Make sure Grunio's color match carrots' color when you catch them. You can change Grunio's color by pressing fire.

166930.overview: An incoming message was received from Military Patrol Vessel Alpha Niner. MPVA9 reported that they were under pirate attack before communications were suddenly cut off. You're going to have to be careful if you want to earn any creds in this sector and you'll need to make deliveries if you want to earn enough to upgrade your ship. Don't forget to check the commodities exchange, there are some deals to be had there.

166931.overview: Gun Runner is based on the classic game Choplifter where you must fly your helicopter over eight side-view, horizontal scrolling levels where the screen scrolls when you move to the left or the right. You must search each level for a certain amount of men within a time limit and when one is seen you must fly as low as you can and lower a winch to pick him up. Trying to stop you are various baddies that fly around each level and must be shot or avoided and if touched or you get shot then you lose one of three lives. You are equipped with three smart-bombs which destroy anything on the screen and you receive one more for every level completed. Also released in Magic Disk 64 1992/12.

167637.overview:
2014 free/public domain vertical scrolling space shooter coded by Roberto Ricioppo and published by The New Dimension.

Guide your drone across the planet of Xiabex and shoot the galaxian empire to pieces. Don't think you drone can survive for long, if you are not careful enough.

167643.overview: An add-on disk for the Commodore 64 version of Gary Kitchen's GameMaker. This version is specific to creating games of the  Science Fiction genre. These include sprites, music, and background elements for loading into GameMaker for creation of your own games.

167645.overview: An add-on disk available for the Commodore 64 version of Garry Kitchen's GameMaker. This one concentrating on Sports and including sprites, music, and background elements for loading into GameMaker for creating sports themed games.

167648.overview: Released in Spain in Tu Micro Commodore Tape #1, part of Tu Micro Commodore magazine.

167669.overview: Only given a very limited release, this cartridge is a collection of four of Geir Straume's minigame competition entries all on one tiny 16KB cart. Including his popular Bell Ringer games (I & II), Diamond Maze 64 and Sub Destroyer.

167674.overview: Go Racing With Peter O'Sullevan allows yourself and seven other players to bet and make money on various horse races on various race courses. Each player starts with £1000 and they can see each horse, their form, trainer and jockey, and their last three races before deciding which horses to bet on. Each player can bet on as many horses as they want and they can bet to win or each-way as well. The race itself is shown form the side at a slight elevated angle and the screen scrolls from right to left with the lead horses. After the race the result is shown and money won / lost for each player before the next race is shown and the betting starts once again.

167683.overview:
Enter the world of great adventures. Take on the role of a speleologist. Gordon Saga is the first self-contained part of a German adventure game series. At the end of this part, you will be asked the great task that the following parts will build upon. 

    All text input and output is in German. This alone distinguishes this game from many others that are mostly written in English. The game even accepts whole sentences. For example, an instruction could be: NIMM DAS SCHWERT UND GEH NACH NORDEN (TAKE THE SWORD AND GO NORTH). If an entry is not understood despite the rather large vocabulary, the computer reports this. Statements he understands but are meaningless at the moment, he ignores. You can, however, if you feel like it, for example, sing, pray or wait, without affecting the gameplay. 

    One of the great things about this adventure game is its variable gameplay. As with the hobbit , you have to be prepared for surprises. Dangers lurk everywhere, the aids are not always found in the same places. Every new attempt to discover the mystery confronts you with new conditions. 

    In some situations it becomes particularly difficult. They are under time pressure. So a door slams shut behind you and the ceiling lowers or a big stone ball rolls towards you. Here, the adventurer has to react quickly and correctly to keep his life. But the fatal accidents are limited. But it can easily happen that a monster steals the most necessary aid and hides it somewhere.

167684.overview:
Golf at the Tower is a Solitaire card  game developed by Maurice Jones and published by Softdisk Publishing, Inc. in the disk magazine Loadstar. Issue #102. This game is the third in Marice Jones' second trilogy of playing-card solitaire games. At last you may shoot par! Golf at the Tower can be called an "impossible" solitaire game. It can be beaten but it is not likely anyone will do it more than a dozen times in a lifetime. That's why I've made this game to be played for score, rather than just for finished games. After all, in golf, does anyone realistically expect to score an 18 on an 18 hole golf-course? 
 
In this version, one simply plays to minimize the number of cards left, even when it is obvious that some will be left. There are strategies that can be employed at various stages of the round. And you can ask the number of cards left, to simplify some decisions. You can still play win-lost\all-nothing if you prefer. Most solid players can get their game down to about a 77 pretty quickly. See how well you can do!

167702.overview:
GRAVITRIX brings arcade-style, mind-bending puzzle-action to your Commodore 64 like never seen before!

Combine stones of four different gravity directions to solve each of the 120 levels across six themed worlds, but be wary of colour changers, conveyor belts, teleporters and other hazards!

To complete each level, you must clear the screen of all of the coloured GRAVITRIX stones. ALL of the stones of EACH colour must be connected in a single 'group' in order for them to vanish, ie. you cannot have multiple, unconnected groups of the same colour in different areas of the screen. The big challenge in GRAVITRIX is that the stones don't just have different colours - they have different 'directions' (or gravity) as well!

Each coloured stone 'falls' in its assigned direction (symbolised by an arrow) whenever there is nothing blocking its path, and this leads to some tricky chain reactions that must be solved. To make your life even harder there is also a time limit, environmental blocks and other gameplay elements that are introduced during the early levels. Supports both PAL and NTSC.

167707.overview:
Produced as a product tie-in with OTA's honey puff cereal, Guldkornexpressen (or Kalaspuffsexpressen) revolves around the brand's bear mascot, who drives a train filled with honey puffs. His task on each level is to pick up boxes of the cereal, add honey and drive the train to the end of the level, where the cargo is loaded into a big box of Guldkorn.

It is not just a straight forward career along the tracks, though. Switches must be set back and forth for the train to go on the right tracks, there are rocks and fallen trees on the track, and you must keep your speed so as not to crash into things. Fortunately for Puff the bear, he has a honeybee friend. By tapping the joystick button, you activate the bee. It is the bee's task to activate the switches and to operate the honey tap. If you hold in the joystick button, you activate an action menu to deal with obstacles. You can choose to jump over fallen trees, throw dynamite at rocks or to let the bear jump out and dig away dirt from the tracks.

168108.overview: A vertical scrolling shooter developed by Vincent Merken using Chris Yates' Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit. Made in 1994, however it was not released until 2003s SEUCK competition. This was the followup to his previous 1993 game Galaxis 9199

171765.overview:
An educational computer game which teaches the locations and names of cities, towns, regions and rivers of Europe.

There are 3 modes, which are Opzoeken (Look up), Overhoring (Quiz), Het Stedenspel (The City Game). The game contains a mid 1980s map of Europe, as evidenced by countries such as East Germany, West Germany, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia. It contains many names and locations of cities, rivers and seas.

In Look Up mode you can type the name of a city or sea and the game will point it out on the map. In Quiz mode, the game will point a randomly selected place and the player must type in the name on time. The helicopter mode is the main part of the game. The player controls a helicopter and must fly to a randomly selected city or location before the time runs out. When the helicopter is close enough to the target city or location, it will turn into a pulsating red dot.

Additionally there is an information browser which shows data per country or a bar graph comparing all countries. The data includes the area in square kilometers, population, agriculture, industry and service industry data.

172010.overview: A Pac-Man clone game published in Home Computing Weekly #044 (10.01.1984).

173194.overview: The aliens from the distant planet Zekloke have established a large military complex on Mars which presents a great threat to Earth. Your job is to sneak into the alien complex and destroy it, but you must also find the plans for a powerful defense shield which are known to be hidden in the complex.

173957.overview:
Genius: Into the Toy Warehouses is a 2016 homebrew platform puzzler written by Daniele Liverani.

The goal is to obtain all the keys in order to open the main door, which also contains an item you must collect. Be careful as some of the rooms have monsters and bombs inside them. Getting to a detonator at least takes care of the bombs.

174624.overview: You will be presented with the Incan Gate and one of the 9 sections does not match the pattern, find it quickly and you can proceed on your journey, fail to find it in time and your journey is over.

174836.overview:
You are above the fabled city to carry out a very daring and dangerous mission: you must in fact recover some priceless platinum diamonds scattered along the underground walls of the undercity. You have to move with the utmost precision, so as not to hit the walls: the slightest contact and your spinning top will explode. Also pay attention to the defense lines prepared by the old ones before their escape from the planet: very powerful lasers, cannons hidden among the rocks, weights that fall along the way that can crush you, etc. Each rumble you recover will give you energy to continue your mission. 
 
Published as Gyroship in Nova Games n.5 (Gennaio 1987).

175388.overview:
Released back in 2006 at the Game Over(view) Freestyle Jam, Greenrunner literally blew the competition away with it's frantic arcade gameplay and amazing mix of sampled speech and high quality soundtrack. It's a game so hardcore and visually intense that it's probable that even Jeff Minter would beg for mercy at the thought of having to beat all 100 levels. Grab a friend (or take on the challenge solo), jump into your Cyanitizer and Yellowizer battle craft, buckle up and warm up the four-directional bug-blasting pesticide cannons. This is going to be one hell of a trip. 

Released by Psytronik in a dual pack with Redrunner.

175407.overview: Galax is a fixed-screen shooter developed by Alan Bond for the Commodore 64 in 1986.

176570.overview:
A text adventure game published as a type-in game in the book "Castles & Kingdoms". 

The Barbarian moved silently through the streets of Belestria, his huge frame dwarfing the Graylock throngs that mingled and flowed from the side-streets. Humans were not an uncommon sight in the Trade City and this one, though larger than most, aroused little attention beyond the ordinary caution taken in the presence of an obviously dangerous being. The Barbarian was called Thoran, which in his own language meant Wolf Slayer. He hailed from the mountains of the far north of the Great Outback, the refuge of the last tribes of Human nomads. He wore no Guildband or armour. Rather, he dressed in traditional loose desert garments. Although his hood partially concealed his features, his bulk betrayed his race to any who might care to examine him more closely. He was intent on his mission. He moved through the streets of the Trade City as though he knew them well. He worked his way amongst merchants, beggars and thieves towards the Palace of the King. His mind and his body were concentrated on a single task. By the time he reached the square opposite the Palace gates he was so preoccupied with his mission that he failed to notice the quiet build-up of troops around him. Not until he heard the twang of a crossbow did he become aware of them. Thoran spun like a cat, whirling to face the direction of the sound. His hand moved so fast it was a blur to the onlookers. He dropped to one knee. Then he rose to his feet again, stretched out his hand in the direction of a young soldier, and opened his clenched fist. The youth who had fired the bolt was one of the youngest and least experienced of the King's garrison. He had done the unforgivable: fired without an order. Although the garrison soldiers didn't flinch, the youth took haIf a step backwards. In Thoran's outstretched hand was the very bolt that had been aimed at him! Thoran shook the hood off his head, revealing decidedly Human features and a shaggy mane of jet-black hair. He moved towards the offending soldier until his outstretched arm was only inches from his face. The air was electric with tension. By Graylock law, Thoran had a right to claim the youth's life for this unprovoked attack. A crowd had gathered by now, and each of the onlookers wondered what would be the outcome of this confrontation between a Human and a Royal Trooper-a rare occurrence in these times of stealth and assassins. Thoran broke into a thunderous laugh; his mirth cracked through the air like a great whip. Lt was not a laugh of ridicule, but one of great amusement. He ripped away his desert garments to reveal the leather dressings of a Hekero, a northern warrior. "l have no quarrel with anyone," he said, loud enough so that all could hear.

177582.overview: An homebrewed Galaxian clone which uses Rob Hubbard's music from the Last V8, and a nice boss level if you can make it that far.

177659.overview:
C64 Game Competition at SEUCK Game Creation Compo 2015 :  Second Place winner. Published in Reset #07 Mix-i-Disk.

You have been selected to test the GIGABLAST -- a devastating new superweapon. Fly the aircraft and drone across the robotic testing field, and take out as many machines as possible.

You control the ship firing lasers, plus a drone which drops Gigablast plasma bombs. Your ship or your drone will be awarded an extra life for every 10,000 points scored. When you come across laser barriers, be careful! They can destroy your ship, but the drone will only be stopped by it. Whenever a green arrow appears on the ground, a hostile force-field will prevent normal flight. You have to pull your ship forward to break out of the field.

177741.overview: Ghosts'n Goblins with modified sprites and levels (after level 2). A sideways scrolling action platformer spread over multiple levels, each of which must be completed within three minutes (or a life is lost), taking in forest, village, mountain and cavern settings with increasing difficulty.

177744.overview: In this adaptation of the traditional board game Gomoku, or Go-Moku, the player can play against the AI. Normal rules apply. Each turn players place their pieces on the board in an attempt to reach five in a row. Rows may be attained horizontally, vertically and diagonally. There are three different AIs to play against a cautious, aggressive and balanced version. The player may also choose to go first or not and which color to play. Published in Loadstar #194.

177818.overview: A scrolling shoot'em up game by Wil Smith, Nik Townes & Ron Burghes created with the SEUCK engine. It features good music, the game is possibly based on the 1988 Firebird Gauntlet style game.

177821.overview: A scrolling shoot'em up and sequel to the original Gothik Attack, based somewhat on Firebird's 1988 Gothik that took original inspiration from Gauntlet. It was created by Wil Smith, Nik Townes & Ron Burghes and released in 1994.

177822.overview: You control a bomb-dropping, LASER shooting chopper and must shoot the ships on the ocean and the attacking UFO's. The game, strangely, leaves access to Commdore Basic open so you can tweak it while you play, if you want. Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1989/02 (Issue #68).

177823.overview: Published in Loadstar #057, this educational Quiz game features a number of fun subjects.

177824.overview: A U.S. geography quiz game published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/03 (Issue #09).

177826.overview: Requires Games Adapter for 4 player use. This is a C64 interpretation of the popular Worms game.

177905.overview: Learn to program and then learn your history, this game was included in book "40 Educational Games for the Commodore 64". Here's a chance to catch up on your history lessons without looking silly getting the answer wrong. With multiple choice answers and the ability to alter and add questions by changing the programming. (When you add questions on line 600-800 make sure to modify lines 70, 80, 110 and 200 to reflect these changes.)

178832.overview: The C64 game based on the 1970's Manga UFO Robo Grendizer called ' Goldrake ', has recently been cracked by Hokuto Force. This game classed as a shoot em up and developed using SEUCK, is inspired by a classic cartoon and features graphics and music by VG VOX.

179281.overview:
The Gold Collection III is a compilation that includes the following games:

Express Raider, 
Supercycle, 
Leviathan, 
Ace of Aces, 
Masters of the Universe: Arcade Version, and
Super Huey II.

179299.overview:
Compilation of racing games including the following 3 games:

•   Championship Sprint
•   Super Hang-On
•   Super Sprint

179460.overview:
Gorilla is an unofficial C64 conversion of the classic old Microsoft QBasic Gorillas game that first came bundled with MS-DOS 5.0. 

It was developed by Marco Timm for the 2009 4K BASIC Compo.

The game is 2 player only.

179464.overview:
Published in Ahoy! 1985/10 (Issue #22). Gravinauts (aka Space Walk in the Caesar Software release) requires you to fight for survival in the hostile environment of the planet Arkion. n the world of Arkion, Survival is a tough business. Because the surface of the planet is covered by a deadly acidic ocean, the inhabitants must remain ontinuously in the air, supported by rocket backpacks. To stay up, they engage in a never-ending war for fuel. The loser is doomed to a very short lifespan. 

The Gravinauts, as they are called by the colonies of the Milky Way, battle each other by trying to reach a higher vantage point in the air than their opponents and smashing into them, destabilizing their gyros and causing their backpacks to explode. 

Because the fuel tanks stored higher up in the atmosphere are more closely guarded, they are entrusted with greater fuel supplies. They are therefore more important than the ones resting on the lower "ice glaciers," which are huge bodies of frozen chemicals floating in the air above the ocean. 
The purpose of the game is to take fuel off the glaciers.

179806.overview: The original version was reworked slightly before being released by Retro Games Ltd. on the THEC64 Mini, but was also available for standard C64 users with these changes at just after Christmas.

179808.overview: Awarded first place in the Mixed Game Competition at Halloween Game Dev Competition 2019 to Digital Monastery!\Hokuto Force. A single button game where you take control of a witch on her broom flying in the skies during Halloween, avoid baddies and collect maximum candies to beat the high score.

180117.overview: A breakout style game known at Squishy: The Game or simply The Game created by Carl Wade. In Italy it was published as both Mattoni and Squeeze.

180407.overview:
Nono Pixie is a Nonogram Puzzle Game for Commodore 64 with 100 unique puzzles to solve! A Nonogram is a puzzle that tells how many squares are in each row and column of a picture. If there are multiple groups in a column or row this is indicated by multiple numbers for the same column or row. 

Released as part of the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2019.

180647.overview:
A 1985 C64 public domain homebrew shooter by Andreas Mettler (Antsoft) .

You are in your cannon and you must shoot down the weird alien creatures before they take you out and take over your planet.

181927.overview: A version of Boulder Dash created by GODS, who were active 1991-1996. There were 47 caves to explore and vanquish in this version!

182236.overview: Created in 2002 by Zoltán Scserbin. The exact same game with different graphics comes under the names Dig Dug Dash 01, Invasion Dash 01, Robot Dash 01 and Auto Dash 01, but is best known by the 2003 naming Golden Boulder - Who Dares Wins 01!

182301.overview: A compilation of 200 caves! Compilation of the best caves of Knibble Dash 1 - 10, where episode 10 is identical to Mrs. Rockford Dash and compiled by Prof. Knibble.

182553.overview: A single screen platformer where the goal is to collect all the gold nuggets in each level to advance, and also watch out for those pesky dragons. It was developed by Harald Furth and published by CA-Verlags GmbH in Commodore Disc #16 and in Italy in COM 64 n.62 (marzo/aprile 1993).

182931.overview: Looks like this version of Boulder Dash is a product of the Gods! Select your starting cave at the select screen and enjoy Boulderfreaks!

182958.overview: 5 new caves, built by the Gods for your Boulder Dashing pleasure.

182979.overview: A homebrew Boulder Dash created by Scserbin Zoltán in 2003 and a sequel to the original. There were 36 in this set of games.

182980.overview: A compilation of various Boulderdash games edited by Prof. Knibble with 200 puzzle caves. Updated and re-released in 2002 with additions by Zoltán Scserbin

183159.overview: Gods Boulder Dash was a series of 9 games released in 1992 with new caves to plunder and puzzles to overcome.

183160.overview: Released by Gods, a new set of caves in this 9 game set.

183178.overview: Created by GODS, this is 6/9 in the boulder dash series.

183181.overview: Fangame written by Gods with the PLCK engine, 7 of 9 in the series.

183182.overview: Created by Gods, this version had 5 new caves to explore.

183183.overview: The final installment of the Gods Boulder Dash series, overall a total of 47 levels.

183187.overview:
Gold Grabber (also called Lode Runner Jr.) is a single-screen platformer developed by Andrew S. Pakerski and published in 1986 by Softalk Production in Loadstar #20. 

There are only about 6 screens in total, however, every time you complete all screens, the screens just repeat and increase in speed every time you have to repeat each screen, so the disappearing platforms speed up every time you play each screen, which makes the game a bit more challenging.

183188.overview: Goldwinner is a public domain slot machine game developed by Bob Mockford for the Commodore 64 in 1990.

183792.overview: Originally released to allow no loss of health, Crackware added next level progression at will and ability to open doors without a key to train on the game and get better. In 2019 an update to it was put out by UDI that fixed NTSC play, added better documentation, a single file implementation and allowed play to level 40.

185294.overview:
The inhabitants of the Delta planet, Zypar are a truly unique people and have a degree of civilization that is unmatched throughout the galaxy. Their laws require that at the age of 18 they must challenge their peers in a special gym to decide their future. The challenge takes place riding an inertial platform with which you have to undermine the opponent or direct him towards the door of death where the photonic rays will disintegrate. Once you have destroyed your opponent you will need to collect his remains to be able to increase your score. You can defend yourself from photonics by taking the energy blocks present in the central hole of the gym. The final winner will be allowed to join the legion of rulers while the loser will have to choose between exile or slavery to the rulers. 

Published in Italy as Gli Sfidanti di Delta (Delta Challengers) in Super Game 2000 n.11 (Gennaio 1986) and Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - super top 30 (1987).

186834.overview:
Guillotine is a horizontal fast-paced scrolling blaster, written by the web master. It was created using Jon Well's Sideways Scrolling adaptation of the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit. The game features two amazing previously released tunes (Title music: Guillotine, In game music: Doom Machine). The front end features additional code, based on the tutorial game Rocket 'n Roll (See SEUCK School).The main idea of this game was based on the music, previously released on Mix Box #10). Guillotine features 3 different levels, with power ups that will enhance the player's shoot ability. The enemy bosses will explode in one go. SEUCK has its own timed feature, but in this game, if the boss explodes before time on a still screen expires. The next level begins.  

INSTRUCTIONS:
You and a friend are pilots of the Interstellar Justice Federation. You have been assigned a very important mission.

An alien Emperor has illegally built a Doom Machine, called the Guillotine. Its purpose is to create a dangerous substance and generate a giant atomic explosive device. The alien forces have been capturing and transporting humans from Earth to the planet of Jetan, and took them to the factory and used them on the machine. The Emperor also threatens to wipe out the universe should it wish to.

Your mission, should you accept it is to enter the planet Jetan, locate the Guillotine and destroy it. However, you will have to fight the alien ships, since a galactic war has also broken out.

There are 3 levels in which you can fight through. They are as follows:

- The Jetan caves
- The factory construction works
- The main entrance to the factory, where you will find the Guillotine.

Luckily our dead pilots left out power pods, which can help you through your mission. They are as follows:

- Red  - Better fire power
- Blue - Matter Splatter explosive
- Green - Bonus lives

Watch out for the bosses at the end of each stage. You'll need a nerve of steel.

Can you thwart the evil Emperor, or will the Universe be forever gone?

Good luck pilots. You will need it.


This game finished third in the 2020 SEUCK Competition.

188498.overview: Compilation of previously released games for easyflash. This time all of them are on one cartridge, supporting both NTSC/PAL.

192401.overview: Welcome to Grid Pix! An exciting new world of logical puzzle solving awaits you. Featuring 100 chunky Picross style pixel-art puzzles (and the option to load in more via future DLC packs), beautiful high-resolution graphics, multiple music tracks to play whilst you think (silence is also optional), PAL/NTSC compatibility and on-cartridge saving! There are no annoying time limits or anything to distract you from the challenge ahead, just 100 hand-pixelled nonograms with only a single solution!

192433.overview: A Brain & Logic game something like Q-Bert. Colour the squares with the hammer while dodging the balls, that randomly turn green allowing you to smash them (like in Pacman). You can also transport to the top-left corner of the screen if surrounded by walking off the right-hand side.  published in 64 Tape Computing No. 03 (1984 / 08-09) and in Go Games n.13 (October 1986) as Hammer.

194619.overview: A one person shooter published as part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack".

199251.overview: The logic puzzle sequel to tease your brain once again. Created by Art Project Studios and published in 64'er 1995/04.

199304.overview: You play a caterpillar that lives in an enclosed garden. In the garden are mushrooms and cherries. You must eat all the cherries that cause you to grow in length while avoiding the mushrooms and walls. If you hit either of those or yourself, you will lose a life and eventually the game will be over. If you manage to eat all the cherries on the screen you will move on to another randomly generated level. Published in France in Hebdogiciel N°023 (16.03.1984), and Hebdogiciel Software N°1.

200572.overview: Ghost-Jail is a text adventure developed and self-published by Dan Byström in 1983. The goal of the game is to escape an evil  jail/prison that is haunted by ghosts before they drive you mad, or you get killed, whichever one comes sooner.

201202.overview:
Glory Quest is a 1-2 player simultaneous game which combines a maze shooter with a collect 'em up style game. This is NOT a co-op game, as you're basically competing against the second player in 2 player mode, not teaming up with the other player. Collect money, food, and health potions and shoot the skull shaped monsters. There are also teleports that teleport you around various areas of the maze, and a vortex which takes you to the next level.

This game was developed by Joe Garrett and published in the following:

•    Loadstar #027
•    Best of Loadstar #3

201942.overview: Gypsy Juggler is a well-made clone of the old 1978 Meadows Games arcade game of the same name. This game was developed in 2021 by Arlasoft and released on his itch.io page.

202001.overview:
An unofficial entry in the Great Giana Sisters franchise, this game was created out of whole cloth by Von Laserdance of Rush using the Shoot'em-up Construction Kit and was released in SYS PD Diskett#45 (1993) and actually published in Italy under several names, including Baby Crazy in Nova Games n.24 (Ottobre 1988).  
 
It isn't a stellar outing for Laserdance as this lacks all the platforming elements beloved in this game and sticks to just the Shooter and collect-em up components.

This is not a typical platform game like Giana, it's actually a SEUCK game in disguise.

202242.overview: Get Out! If You Can is a 2D style maze game which was developed in 1988 by Matthew Wiseman. It was published by Softdisk Publishing in UpTime Vol.1 #10.

205370.overview:
Psytronik Software is proud to present another exciting release from Karl Hörnell - author of C64 classics like Clean Up Service, Fungus, Velocipede and more recently, Iceblox Plus! In his latest game, GRAVITON you have to use your powers of dexterity to steer a ball through a maze. Careful reactions and precise control are necessary to successfully navigate the mazes.

 ** THE GAME ** 

Guide the ball along the path through the maze by tilting the board and letting gravity do the work.

Try not to fall into the holes! The further you go, the more points you get.

An indicator on the right shows which way the board is currently tilted.

Focus on precise and gentle joystick motion! It may take some time getting used to.


** FEATURES ** 

· 20 challenging maps to navigate through

· Sleek clean visuals

· Responsive controls

· Silky smooth scrolling

· Atmospheric soundtracks

· TheC64 Mini/Maxi compatible


** CREDITS ** 

Programmed by Karl Hörnell

Graphics and Game Design by Karl Hörnell

Music by Hans Axelsson-Svala & Alexander Danielsson

Packaging Artwork by Karl Hörnell

Additional Packaging Design by Jason ‘Kenz’ Mackenzie

Tape Mastering by Richard Bayliss & Martin Piper

© 2021 Eweguo aka Karl Hörnell

205421.overview:
Gremlin Hunt is a brain/memory game in which you have to find  and pair up gremlins (they look more like fairies or pixies) hiding inside flowers.

The game was developed by LITAG Productions and published in Loadstar #77.

205491.overview:
If you ever believed that fast 3D space action on the C64 was a case of flickering wireframe - well, you are in for a treat.

“Gates of the ANCIENT” offers full polygon 3D exploration, battle and looting on your trusty old C64.

Explore a series of systems and galaxies, stringed together with wormhole technology.  Upgrade your ship with various devices and use ancient artifacts.  Fight pirates, aliens and ancient robots to keep alive in a hostile universe – or become a pirate yourself and take it from the rich.

Every game is different, but a codeword system allows you to bring you worldly possessions into your next incarnation. So you can build up your ship to reach the final goal over many sessions. 

 Optimized for C64 PAL - but will run on NTSC (maybe a little too fast).. Vesion 1.01 will now also work with accelerators such as SuperCPU.

205775.overview:
Galaxian DX is an unofficial conversion of the 1979 arcade classic, Galaxian. It was developed by Nick "Arlasoft" Sherman and released on his itch.io page on October 23, 2021. 

Game description:

Galaxian is a shoot 'em up in which the player is at the bottom of the screen, with an arrangement of aliens at the top. The player moves left and right to aim at an alien, then shoots a bullet up the screen, and the alien it hits is killed. The aliens are classed as Drones, Emissaries, Hornets and Commanders, with those higher up the screen scoring more points when destroyed. At set intervals an enemy will move down the screen towards you, escorting a bomber, which is a moment of high danger. Clear a wave and another is generated.

207444.overview: The Great Washing Machine King is a rather surreal game for the Commodore 64 in the same mold as games like Manic Miner or Jet Set Willy, except a bit weirder and with less platforming. The game was developed by the team at Digital Monastery (the game development division of cracking/demo group Hokuto Force), and was released into the public domain on December 12, 2020.

208575.overview: Gamblers-Delight is a slot machine game developed by Robert Young and Paul Copeland for the Commodore 64. It was released as a type-in program in the book The Penguin Book of Commodore 64 Games in 1983.

208652.overview: Created with an early version of the Gyroscope-Maker\Gyroscope Construction Set by Electro and The Floppy Runner of the Electronic Cracking Crew.

208658.overview: Create your own Gyroscope levels and trade them with your friends. Collect the levels and make your own game!

209025.overview:
Your spacecraft is caught in the middle of a beautiful but deadly meteor shower. As ship commander can you survive? A challenging space game with outstanding graphics. 

As you glide through outer space, meteors of many colors swirl past your spaceship. You'd like to stop and watch the display, but you better keep moving — a collision with a meteor means the end of your ship. If you act fast, you can dodge the meteors and ward them off with your ship's photon gun. 

Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/07 (Issue #37), and also in Stonysoft #0343

209060.overview:
An April Fool's Day joke of a game for the youngsters that want to try TGGS without many baddies. Spoofing popular Junior edition games for introductory level playing. It still manages to have some difficult spots and is a decent into into the game mechanics for someone who never mastered TGGS back in the day. 
 
After falling into a dark, deep sleep, little GIANA finds herslef in a mysterious dreamworld where everything is strange and ...FORGET IT! 
 
Have fun little dwarves, now play your own special Giana Sisters without any pressure, feel free to cheat if you want. High Score saver is disabled if cheatmode is ON.  
 
33 levels, just like the first one. It is getting darker and darker and every fourth level is a cave by night. Creepy isn't it?! High scores will be saved automatically. If you become a pro, teach your parents to play. Then take a break and go out and see the sun. Go Outside and play with friends, have fun in the real world. Welcome to The Great Giana Sisters Junior!

209163.overview: A Game and Watch Homage, where you are a boy living in an apartment with two floors, and the only way to enjoy his hobby of playing with balls, is by bringing them downstairs. The only problem is, today of all days is 'Granny's Cleaning Day'. Pick up the balls and bring them downstairs as fast as possible, avoid Granny's powerful hoover, make sure she doesn't suck up your hobby, and use the phone to distract her and change her direction. So good luck, as you only have a limited amount of lives!

209201.overview: Giant and Dwarfs is a strategical board game for one or two players for the Commodore 64. It was developed and released by Remsoft Systems in 1988.

209234.overview:
Gems is a 1992 single player Columns clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Chris McDermott and published in the following:

•     Loadstar #101
•     Game Star #1

209235.overview:
Gold Train is a 1991 vertically scrolling wild west themed shoot 'em up for the Commodore 64. You play a cowboy on horseback trying to protect a train from various enemies.

The game is somewhat similar to the old 1982 Taito arcade game "Wild Western"

This game was developed by David Shepherd, Dominic Taylor & Richard Taylor and published in Your Commodore 1991/09 (Tape #21),

209236.overview:
Golden Age is a game in which you play a caveman. Your goal is to catch eggs dropped by a dragon to feed your family. Avoid the red ones, as they are actually fireballs. You also have to contend with scorpions on the ground by jumping over them when they cross the screen.

This game was developed in Italy by Pietro Pino and published in the following:

•     Commodore 64 Club #08 [Italian Release]
•     Commodore Computer Club Nr.6 [v1+v2]
•     Alga Soft 1989 n.4b

210288.overview:
Grime is an old DOS game I used to have on my PC XT... it was a simple little text game, that was a lot of fun!

Grime was written by Mark Elendt... as far as I remember I got it from an old magazine coverdisk...

currently Grime is 'abandonware'... no one seems to really remember it, and it's trickyto get working on a modern pc, as it runs too fast!!..

At the start of July 2018, I started a 7 day programming project to recreate 'Grime' as a Z80 based game... I chose it because it's fun and simple, and this gave me a good opportunity... I wasn't just going to remake Grime... I was going to make it work on 11 different systems!

I remade grime as  'Grime Z80' which uses one piece of logic code that plays on 11 different Z80 systems... namely: Amstrad CPC, ZX Spectrum,MSX1, MSX2, Enterprise, Sam Coupe, TI-83 calculator, Gameboy, Gameboy Color, Sega Mastersystem and Sega Gamegear!

But why stop there... I now had a simple game 'template' which could be extended for something new... why just limit it to the Z80? so in December 2018 I started the project again... this time as Grime 6502

210289.overview:
After the Craptastic Compo release in 2016, and a joke full release during the same year. During the Summer of 2020, The New Dimension is pleased to announce a complete full game with a proper loading bitmap, title screen and different sub level screens to play on each level.  Granny's Teeth has finally become a full game. Released now :)

This game works on PAL and NTSC machines and is also fully compatible with theC64 mini/full size computer.

Poor old Granny Hegarty. She was looking after her grandchildren until it was bed time. She gently tucked them in to bed, and went to bed herself - dropping the false teeth into a glass by her bed side. Alas, the next morning comes by. Granny wakes up and finds that her teeth are missing. It turns out that the children got up early and played hide and seek with them and chucked the teeth in to a fish bowl. The kids also ransacked Granny's house. Raffles the dog has been set loose, and Tiddles, the cat is on the prowl. ... and who let that toy plane, spider and giant wasp in to the house? Also little did Granny know was that her house was built above a swimming pool.

Your task is to help poor old Granny retrieve her teeth by locating them from the fish bowl. Watch out for the animals and insects, and other hazards. If you hit any hazards, you will lose a life and be thrown back to the start of each level.

210290.overview:
Daniele Liverani has announced the immediate availability of his latest version of the Genius Series arcade games for the Apple II . Genius 3 – Into The Toy Planets is a major continuation of the theme Daniele began more than 5 years ago.

Each game that Daniele produces comes with not only the Game Disk in Apple II emulator ready format .DSK, but also a PDF instruction manual, a 5.25 inch floppy disk label PDF as well as a tip document entitled Secrets for the users who get stuck in the game.

210366.overview:
An original fun hi score party game written for the CSDB Fun Compo 2021.

Do you remember the classic seaside, fairground arcade machines where you insert a coin into the slot, and control a remote-controlled water boat, bumper car or something like that around the track?

The New Dimension has gone one step further is very proud to present a pretty original hi score attack party game called Gyro Run. A silly game in which you control a moving spinner around the arena attempting to score as many points as you can.

The goal of the game is to grab as many tasty treats that spawn into the arena at random. Also objects can also spawn into a different object. These objects will give points (200, 300 or 500). The treats will also award the spinner a temporary shield which is short lived.

If the spinner crashes into the deadly skulls without a shield (or the shield just run out) a life is lost. It is also possible that treats or skulls will spawn on exactly the same spot as your spinner.  It is best to keep the shield up and running. After approximately 45 seconds, a smart bomb will appear. Pick one of these to clear the arena.

Controlling of the spinner is completely different. There  is a dial at the bottom of the screen, which can be turned to 8 directions, clockwise or anti-clockwise. The spinner can only change direction via the fire button control.

The game took first place in the game's portion of the competition

210367.overview: Way back in 2006 a coder by the name of Widdy released a rather charming little game called Beer Belly Bill In : Grillieren! Barbecue Deluxe for the Gameboy Advanced, with later ports to the Wii, Android and even Java. But now in 2017 Widdy(Code/Graphics) and FieserWolf (Music) via Genesis Project, has released a preview of the C64 version, which according to a CSDb member by the name of Groepaz is about 10 years old!

210516.overview: A pong style game created by Richard Hezseltine and published in Zzap!64 Megatape #22.

211250.overview: An arcade style pinball game for you C64 from Loadstar for 1 to 4 players, created by Gus Vakalis and released in Loadstar #139. The game includes all the flashing lights and buzzing bumpers of the real arcade game plus a screen designer to make your own pinball tables.

211385.overview: We've certainly heard a lot about that famous platformer the Great Giana Sisters from 1987, especially as it came back to the Amiga as a Giana Special Edition by Reimagine Games and then of course the Great Giana-Sisters Construction-Set, whereby you can create your own levels. But this latest release as The Great Giana PETSCII Sisters on the C64 by Vintage Computing Carinthia, is something of a special breed and one you might be interested in checking out! With graphics by Logiker and coding by Will, this is a brand new release for the C64 in which much of the game has been remade in PETSCII graphics by Vintage Computing Carinthia released at Revision 2022 Online!

213286.overview: A 3D dungeon crawler where you play the role of a brave dwarven hero. In it you craft your own here and experience another adventure in the Kingdom of Roglia, the land of the dwarves. This adventure takes place in the Curious Dimor Mine, which is located deep in the south of the dwarf kingdom Roglia. Every dwarf knows that there are still vast amounts of gold pieces and gemstones in this old mine. When the dwarf people waged a war against the hungry ogres of Traublonia nearly 200 years ago, every weapons-capable dwarf was needed at the front, and there were no longer any smaller mines and guards left in Dimor. After the army of the small people was able to achieve a glorious victory in the legendary battle of Kharakon and thus ended the war, some of the invaders took up residence in these unguarded mines and it will be your job to expel them. In short, Gold Quest VI is all about accumulating as many points for the high score as possible. To this end, you must fight deeper and further into the veins of the mine and collect as much gold as possible. Finally, if you encounter the boss boss boss shaman or its dragon, you can take up the fight with him. If this is victorious, the curse is taken from the mine and Sledgie can be freed from captivity. The gold aprons of Roglia can resume their work and the player is included in the Great Book of Dwarven Heroes.

213302.overview:
Gold Swappers is a board game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jim Green and released into the public domain in 1989. It was coded entirely in BASIC.

Description:

Well, you see, there were these two guys and each had four gold coins. Problem is, both were greedy and wanted all of them, so they played this game. It is played by moving the gold (represented by the small yellow circles/dots) between four boxes. Each box starts off with  two pieces of gold. In turn, the players take the gold from one of their boxes and distribute it counterclockwise to the other three boxes.

There will always be at least one empty box, because during each move gold cannot be put back into the box from which it was taken.

To win the game and satisfy your greed, you must get all the gold in one of your own boxes.

213314.overview: The Gold Icon is a public domain text adventure for the Commodore 64. The developer are currently unknown. The game was released on the ICPUG Adventure Disc #1.

213360.overview:
Garten Eden (also released in The Netherlands as Appel Vangen) is a German language "catch it" game similar to games like Kaboom. Except this time, you play a farmhand who must catch the apples falling from the tree. Misd too many, and you will be fired.

Originally published in Happy Computer 1984/07. Then released by Courbois Software in Courbois Software #6430

213375.overview: The Guardians of Arimathea is a selectable answers adventure game with a fantasy theme for the Commodore 64. It was developed by David Estall and published in 1984 as a type-in game in the book "Adventures for the Commodore 64".

214717.overview:
The award-winning multi game for the Commodore C=64 by Welle: Erdball. The German language game GEHIRN-ANALYSE (Brain Analysis)!
The beta version won the first prize at the WILLOW Party 2004 in Wellentrup, Germany. Test your brain abilities with up to 4 players and the possibility to enter the list of famous brains. Prove your mental ability in calculating, word pool, photographic mind, reaction and strategy in 9 disciplines.

215338.overview: A scrolling space shooter created by Martijn Schutten, Nikaj Eijk and Elvin Van Lvyk (of Electric Brains Productions) for one or two players, according to the title screen it was published in 1993 by Commodore Force Magazine. In fact, while the dev team had already done Relax and Battle Bars for Commodore Force, oddly CF didn’t end up publishing this neat little shooter done for them in 1993 in the magazine.

215340.overview: A primitive space vessel simulation created by Peter R. Boothman and released in Loadstar #189. A full 1541 full of interstellar trade, interspersed with encounters with space bandits. In it you are a galactic middleman. After years of saving you have finally raised enough cash to purchase a stat of the art spaceship. It's 2543 AD and trading can be a a profitable business in the Astron Galaxy. You have 1000 gold pieces and you have purchased an old style laser gun and a standard missile bay with 4 missiles. You start at space station Lazarus. Use the joystick or keyboard to pick menu options. Use the joystick to choose the heading (of 8 directions) and fire or spacebar to engage. Acceleration and deceleration is manual. Use Command to check status of ship and hyperspace drive (if you can ever save up for one).  Approach a planet and when the S icon turns white it means you have found a space station in orbit and can trade, refuel, repair or take a shuttle to the planet. You can even refuel your hyperspace drive!

215341.overview: A golf game for 1-4 players from Nathan Tennies & Thomas N. Hayes and released by Gamestar in a line of golf games that they would continue into the DOS days of the late 80's.

215342.overview: Released in 1990 by Markt & Technik/64'er and created by Wolfgang Ring, published in 64'er Sonderheft 60. Find the pharaoh's tomb in the dark catacombs of the Cheops Pyramid. Where is the king's legendary death mask?

215343.overview: Das Geheimnis der Pyramiden or The Mystery of the Pyramids is a public domain text adventure game with selectable answers created by Karlheinz Herpel and released in Digital Marketing PD #157 and in 64´er - 78 Paradize.

215344.overview: A German language, mixed challenge game with wordsearch and a simple quiz game for one to four players created by Hannes Malecki of Welle Erdball and released as part of the mixed Competition at Willow Party 2005 where it came in second place, it comes with some very nice music. It was also released in GO64! 2005/08. This game is the second part in a trilogy of games.

215345.overview: A German language, four person party quiz created by Hannes Malecki and released at Willow Party 2006, where it placed first in the mixed competition and also in GO64! 2006/06.

215346.overview: A Yahtzee style game created by Miguel Grinberg for one to four players, it was released in Spanish sometime in the mid to late 80's.. English language support was added unofficially.

215347.overview: A Dutch 3D platformer released in 1983 by HPF in Digital Marketing PD #151 and by Courbois Software #6415.  It is something of a Q-bert clone with some cheery jingles. It was later released in German in 1984.

215348.overview:
An action game released by André Vuegteveen, Andre Schroeder and music by Voicetracker (as a group, The Rough Arts) in both 64'er Sonderheft 97, and in 64'er 1997/11. Game has 3 modes of difficulty. You are a flashing animated ball and your duty is to get the flashing key. Sounds easy, but you may not touch the other sprites and there is a time limit to be considered. When you get the key (displayed in the GFX) you have to go to the door and press fire there. Then 3 other doors appear and you have to choose the correct one.  
 
If you choose the wrong door, the same happens as when you touch and enemy sprite or when the time runs out before you get the key. You lose one of your 3 lives. Choosing correctly takes you to the next level. If you can get past all 10 levels you get a nice end game sequence.

215349.overview: An action Pong style variant game for two competing players created for Revision 2017 by Tim Scharrenborg. In this game player 1 controls the paddles while player 2 controls the ball. A little twist and the fun begins!

215455.overview: Western-themed shooter game created by Outlaw-Emix Software using SEUCK. Loops to the start after completing. Shoot the train cars and the dangerous cowboys that have their sites set on taking you out. Game can be played by one or two players and cooperatively.

215457.overview:
Bizarre Dutch game. Seems the objective is to just get all the pesky critters away from your garden.

Created and published in 1985 by Esther Brand, with music by Harry Bratt, B. Retelle & J. Brady, lifted from the music from the first Star Wars film.

216128.overview:
A game created by Tim Hartnell & Brett Hale and published in 1984 in the book "The Big Fat Book of Commodore 64 Games". The computer plays a mean hand in this electronic version of the well-known card game. The aim of the game is to build up a series of 'books', where a book is all four of a particular card (such as four Aces, or four nines).
You start the game with five cards each. You can see your cards but (of course) you cannot see the computer's hand. The two players take it in turns to ask their opponents tor a particular card which they need to help build up a set. If the player being asked does not have a requested card, the 'asker' must GO FISH (that is, select a card from those which have not been dealt).

216438.overview: Ghost'n Goblins 1994 is a ROM hack of the official C64 conversion of Ghosts'n Goblins. The graphics have been slightly modified and the gameplay has also been slightly modified as well. This hack was made by Adam Englund in 1994.

216439.overview: Ghoul Gobbler is a homebrewed Pac-Man clone for the Commodore 64. The developer and year of release are currently unknown.

217711.overview: A dice gambling game for 1 to 8 players created by Günter Kramer and published in Commodore Disc #41.

219201.overview: A SEUCK based western shooter for one by Sonny Top. Avoid the cactus and the cow pies and all the lead filling the air as you make your way through the wilderness and into town to cut down the desperadoes through the haze of gun-smog that fills the air.

219215.overview: In this game you're a bull in a field. Quick - before the farmer can shoot you, you should impregnate all of his cows! Avoid the crosshairs. Move onto cows to increase your "score". Maybe in the end it is all about the love you make, we'll all be hamburger someday.

219442.overview: This board game variant, created by David M. Moorman and published in Loadstar #123 was published in 1994. This two-player game of chess puts you on a spherical board with twice as many pieces. Watch your back! Played on a 16x8 board with wrap-around east/west movement. Each side has 32 pieces, with for each rooks, knights, and bishops. Pawns come in 2 varieties: east bound and west bound. Two new pieces have been added, the Princess who moves like a queen but only up to 3 steps and the prince who moves like a queen for two steps OR makes a knight's move.

219573.overview:
Arlasoft tackled the complexity of making a faithful rendering of the Famicom port of  arcade game and released his version in 2021 and has continued to update it, adding 2-Player cooperative mode, pause and has worked to make it all look as close to the original as possible.  Galaga is a vertical arcade shooter. You control a space fighter at the bottom of the screen, scrolling left and right in order to avoid oncoming bombs and kamikaze attacks from alien invaders--and to fire your own missiles to fight back!

There are a huge amount of stages to progress through. Every third level is a "challenge stage" in which you have a free chance to shoot as many aliens as possible and rack up bonus points.

Certain aliens have tractor beams they can use to capture one of your ships. If that wasn't your last "life," you can try to shoot that alien down and recapture your ship, giving you two ships at once and doubling your firepower.

278308.overview:
Galactic Quarry X is a 2019 side scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jari Karjalainen and released by TND.

The year is 205X. The off-world mining company Royal Space Mining Corp. has finished unloading their last shipment of unknown ore found on Planet X. Suddenly, a fleet of unknown origin enter the planet's orbit, and RSMC's mining equipment is still waiting to be picked up at the last quarry.

Commander Fotheringay-Phipps of the Royal Galactic Task Force sends three of his most disposable pilots to deal with the unexpected menace and bring back the mining equipment from the quarry on Planet X. If they fail, the mission is aborted, the RSMC mothership returns to base on Earth and faces the consequences,whatever they may be.

279821.overview: Guns'n'Roses is a 1-2 player (co-op) wild west/cowboys vs. Indians style shoot em up for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Albert Pluns & Peter Vandeale using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, and published by Cult Design Studio in 1992.

295001.overview: A PD single-screen arcade platformer from Daniele Liverani and released in 2017.  You play as a European prince who is trapped in a world of dreams. Find all the keys, unlock all the secret caverns and collect all the toys.

417638.overview:
A game published in the ReRun Special Summer Edition 1990. 
 
SMELL THE BURNING RUBBER as your go-cart careens around the perilous curves! Go-Carts, an arcade-style racing game, pits you against a number of computerized drivers. The object is to earn points by passing the other go-carts on the curvy road.
A joystick plugged into port 2 is used to accelerate, decelerate and steer. You must time each pass perfectly and accurately adjust your speed to the radius and slope of each curve; on the really sharp ones, you should slow down to around 30 to avoid sliding into traffic. When the road curves to the right, pass in the right lane; when the road curves to the left, pass in the left lane. Every cart passed is worth five points.
You start the race with five go-carts, which race one at a time. Whenever your cart collides with another or runs out of time, it disappears. However, you won't lose a cart that has passed at least 29 others in a single race.

A race lasts 60 seconds. You can pause the action by pressing the space bar and restart it by pressing the Fl key. As you race, the track moves down in front of you in 3-D fashion and mountains scroll in the background. In spite of all this action, the screen update is as rapid as the monitor raster rate itself.

417961.overview: A single player SEUCK based shooter created by Jan Maly with music by Richard Bayliss. in 2008 a deluxe version would be released.

425392.overview:
Gomoku, also called Five in a Row, is an abstract strategy board game. It is traditionally played with Go pieces (black and white stones) on a 15×15 Go board  while in the past a 19×19 board was standard. Because pieces are typically not moved or removed from the board, gomoku may also be played as a paper-and-pencil game. The game is known in several countries under different names. This version was released by Stefan Wessels in 2023 for multiple 8 bit computers. 

Players alternate turns placing a stone of their color on an empty intersection. Black plays first. The winner is the first player to form an unbroken line of five stones of their color horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. In some rules, this line must be exactly five stones long; six or more stones in a row does not count as a win and is called an overline. If the board is completely filled and no one has made a line of 5 stones, then the game ends in a draw.  
 
The game plays a decent game of Gomoku on Hard AI. The medium and easy modes can be very easy - good for younger kids. If left at a menu or splash screen, the game will time-out and return to the splash screen from where it will start a demo mode. The demo mode is just two AIs of random skill playing against one-another.
